title: GST 111 (COOU) | Chapter Six: Reading Skills and Reading Comprehension for Effective Communication
subject: GST 111

questions.question: Reading is one of the four language skills and like writing, it is a?
questions.explanation: Reading, like writing, is a complex exercise which must be learned.

questions.question: According to Okeke (2015), reading involves a developmental process which can never be completely?
questions.explanation: Reading involves a developmental process which can never be completely mastered.

questions.question: Okeke (2015) sees reading as a skill that cannot be mastered once and for all, yet is the basic tool for?
questions.explanation: Reading is the basic tool for learning, even though it cannot be mastered once and for all.

questions.question: Reading efficiency and reading comprehension are?
questions.explanation: Reading efficiency and reading comprehension are inter-related.

questions.question: According to Agbeha (2003), reading is simply the meaningful interpretation of?
questions.explanation: Agbeha (2003) defines reading as the meaningful interpretation of graphic signs.

questions.question: Maduekwe (2007) defines reading as an activity in which the eyes, the mind and the brain interact in the process of perceiving, analysing, reasoning, interpreting and?
questions.explanation: Maduekwe (2007) defines reading as involving perceiving, analysing, reasoning, interpreting and integrating a problem.

questions.question: Reading can be defined as searching for the thought that was in the mind of the?
questions.explanation: Reading can be defined as searching for the thought that was in the mind of the author.

questions.question: An efficient reader is he who looks for what thought that lies beneath the?
questions.explanation: An efficient reader looks for the thought that lies beneath the printed words.

questions.question: According to Maduekwe (2007), reading is a creative art because it involves a reader's ability to make meaning out of?
questions.explanation: Reading is a creative art because it involves a reader's ability to make meaning out of instructions, newspaper articles, novels etc.

questions.question: Reading is described as interaction because it can take place only when there is some kind of interaction between a reader and the?
questions.explanation: Reading is interaction since it takes place only when there is interaction between a reader and the words on a printed page.

questions.question: According to Maduekwe (2007), reading is interpretation which implies making sense out of something that one has?
questions.explanation: Reading is interpretation, implying making sense out of something that one has read.

questions.question: Reading is also described as a social act because there exists a relationship between a reader and a?
questions.explanation: Reading is a social act because there exists a relationship between a reader and a text.

questions.question: Reading is responding because a reader cannot read a text?
questions.explanation: Reading is responding because a reader cannot read a text passively but tries to respond or react to the writer's ideas.

questions.question: According to Uwadiegwu (2007), one purpose of reading is to acquire information or?
questions.explanation: Uwadiegwu (2007) itemises purposes of reading as to acquire information or knowledge, for vocabulary acquisition and for exam purpose.

questions.question: Onukwugha (1999) adds that one can read for?
questions.explanation: Onukwugha (1999) adds that one can read for pleasure, such as poems, novels, comic strips and cartoons.

questions.question: The whole reading process can be divided into pre-reading, intensive and?
questions.explanation: The whole reading process is divided into pre-reading, intensive and interpretative reading.

questions.question: Setting a clear purpose for reading a text is part of?
questions.explanation: Establishing purpose is part of preparing to read.

questions.question: If your purpose of reading is to obtain specific information, you do not study the text but you?
questions.explanation: If the purpose is to obtain specific information, you scan the text to locate the required information.

questions.question: Anticipating the content of a text may be done by?
questions.explanation: Anticipating the content of a text may be done by questioning.

questions.question: Identifying the main idea is done by?
questions.explanation: Identifying the main idea is done by skimming.

questions.question: Skimming is an important skill that a reader employs to get the general impression or ______ of a text.
questions.explanation: Skimming is employed to get the general impression or main idea of a text.

questions.question: According to Maduekwe (2007), skimming serves the purpose of finding references, locating new materials and obtaining general idea of the?
questions.explanation: Skimming serves to find references, locate new materials and obtain general idea of the information.

questions.question: Skimming may be defined as the fastest reading rate possible that enables the reader to cover large materials in a remarkable short?
questions.explanation: Onukwugha (1999) defines skimming as the fastest reading rate possible that enables the reader to cover large materials in a remarkable short time.

questions.question: Scanning is a skill that the reader requires for locating ______ information in a text without actually reading it.
questions.explanation: Scanning is used for locating specific information in a text without actually reading it.

questions.question: Agbeha (2003) traces the causes of students' poor reading habits to the many years of poor?
questions.explanation: Agbeha (2003) traces the causes of students' poor reading habits to the many years of poor teaching to which they have been exposed.

questions.question: Poor visual perception may be caused by the phenomenon of visual?
questions.explanation: Poor visual perception may be caused by the phenomenon of visual illusion whereby a familiar word is perceived instead of the actual word.

questions.question: Vocalization is a tendency to speak to oneself while?
questions.explanation: Vocalization is a tendency to speak to oneself while reading.

questions.question: Sub-vocalization involves a tendency to pronounce the words ______ as they read.
questions.explanation: Sub-vocalization involves pronouncing words internally as they read.

questions.question: Regression is a tendency to re-read a sentence or phrase immediately it has been read before going to read the?
questions.explanation: Regression is a tendency to re-read a sentence or phrase before going to read the next sentence.

questions.question: Word-by-word reading indicates poor recognition?
questions.explanation: Word-by-word reading indicates poor recognition span.

questions.question: Inflexibility means a failure to adjust one's reading speed to suit the reading material and the reader's?
questions.explanation: Inflexibility means failure to adjust reading speed to suit the reading material and the reader's purpose.

questions.question: Which reading speed is adopted when the reader reads slowly and aims at high comprehension to retain information?
questions.explanation: Study speed is adopted when the reader reads slowly and aims at high comprehension to retain information.

questions.question: Average speed comes in-between slow study speed and?
questions.explanation: Average speed comes in-between slow study speed and skimming/scanning.

questions.question: Skimming is ideal for novel reading, especially reading it for?
questions.explanation: Skimming is ideal for novel reading, especially reading it for pleasure rather than for examination purpose.

questions.question: Poor readers tend to move their heads from one point of the book to another when only the ______ should be used.
questions.explanation: Poor readers move their heads when only the eyes should be used rapidly to recognise the printed material.

questions.question: Pointing of finger to individual words slows down reading speed just like?
questions.explanation: Pointing of finger slows down reading speed just like head movement.

questions.question: Reading comprehension means understanding the writer's?
questions.explanation: Reading comprehension means understanding the writer's meanings.

questions.question: Ifechelobi (2011) defines reading comprehension as a thinking process which entails reasoning, evaluations, speculations, guesses and?
questions.explanation: Ifechelobi (2011) defines reading comprehension as a thinking process entailing reasoning, evaluations, speculations, guesses and interpretations of an author's point of view.

questions.question: A technique used in discovering the meaning of difficult or unfamiliar words in a written material is known as?
questions.explanation: Word analysis is a technique used in discovering the meaning of difficult or unfamiliar words.

questions.question: The core of a word is called?
questions.explanation: The core of a word is called root.

questions.question: Affixes that appear before a word are called?
questions.explanation: Affixes that appear before a word are called prefixes.

questions.question: Affixes that appear after a word are called?
questions.explanation: Affixes that appear after a word are called suffixes.

questions.question: According to Anumihe and Kalu-Nwiwu (2000), a good reader should acquire extensive?
questions.explanation: Anumihe and Kalu-Nwiwu (2000) explain that a good reader should acquire extensive vocabulary to read and interpret meanings of words correctly.

questions.question: Extensive reading is a type of reading we do during leisure to familiarise ourselves with a wide variety of?
questions.explanation: Extensive reading is done during leisure to familiarise ourselves with a wide variety of reading matter.

questions.question: Which of these is a benefit of reading widely?
questions.explanation: Reading widely increases your reading speed, among other benefits.

questions.question: Intensive reading involves carefulness and adequate concentration with slow reading speed in order to achieve?
questions.explanation: Intensive reading involves carefulness and adequate concentration with slow reading speed to achieve accuracy.

questions.question: Turning-in is the ability of a reader to prepare in order to be effectively?
questions.explanation: Turning-in is the ability of a reader to prepare in order to be effectively involved.

questions.question: Scanning is the reading skill which enables the reader to discover?
questions.explanation: Scanning enables the reader to discover specific information only.

questions.question: Which of these is a guideline to an effective comprehension exercise?
questions.explanation: Cross-checking is one of the guidelines to an effective comprehension exercise.

questions.question: Cross-checking will help a reader to commit to memory relevant points and to ______ information which has been obtained.
questions.explanation: Cross-checking helps a reader to commit to memory relevant points and to recall information obtained.
